sections.h2: Where do I take Dent County property tax questions?
sections.html:
Most Dent County tax offices share the courthouse at 400 N. Main Street in Salem, MO 65560. The Assessor, Alisa Brookshire, is at 573-729-6010 or dentcountyassessor@gmail.com. The Collector of Revenue, Shannon VanKirk, is at 573-729-3911. Both offices are open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., closed on major holidays. The County Clerk, Angie Curley, at 573-729-4144, schedules Board of Equalization appointments. The Recorder of Deeds, Cindy Ard, is at 112 E. Fifth Street, Suite 2, phone 573-729-2198.

The Collector's page explains the split: the Assessor values taxable property, and the Collector sends out bills, takes payments and distributes the money. The Collector also processes escrow payments from mortgage holders. Tax statements can be viewed and paid online through dentcountycollector.com, and the Assessor offers a GIS map where you can look up parcels by address, owner name or parcel number.

sections.h2: When does Dent County mail and collect real estate tax?
sections.html:
Dent County real estate and personal property bills are mailed by November 8 each year and are due by December 31. Penalty starts on January 1. The Collector distributes the money to 22 political subdivisions with certified levies, a group that includes schools, roads and fire districts, and also collects tax on state assessed utilities such as railroads, pipelines and electric lines.

  • Pay by December 31 to avoid penalty, and ask the Collector for the current penalty schedule if you are late.
  • Homeowners with a mortgage escrow account should confirm that the lender received the bill.
  • Personal property is separate: listings go to the Assessor between January 1 and March 1, and a late listing can bring a penalty up to $105.00.
  • Anyone moving in from another Missouri county should bring a last paid personal property receipt to set up an account.

If you sell a house, ask the Collector how to report the new owner's name and mailing address, or have the title company do it, so the next bill goes to the right person.

sections.h2: How is a house in Dent County assessed?
sections.html:
The Assessor values all taxable property as of January 1, the statutory assessment date, and tracks over 11,000 parcels. Real estate falls into three subclasses: residential at 19% of market value, agricultural at 12% of production value and all other property at 32% of true value in money. Reassessment occurs every two years in odd-numbered years, and new construction and additions are added every year.

At the county's median home value of $167,500, the 19% residential rate gives an assessed value near $31,825. The tax then equals that figure divided by 100 and multiplied by the combined levy of the districts serving the parcel. Ask the Assessor or Collector for the levy on your own parcel.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Dent County valuation?
sections.html:
Start with the Assessor's office and ask how the value was reached. The Assessor must follow State Tax Commission oversight, which includes monthly visits by field representatives and annual spot reviews. If that conversation does not settle it, take the appeal to the Board of Equalization. RSMo 137.275 sets the deadline at the second Monday in July.

The County Clerk schedules those hearings. Under RSMo 138.060, the board decides appeals in a summary way, and nothing presumes the assessor's valuation is correct. For a property whose assessed valuation rose by 15% or more over the previous assessment, other than because of new construction or improvements, the assessor must prove the value does not exceed true market value. Bring last cycle's notice, photos and any recent appraisal or sale evidence.

Appeals to the State Tax Commission must come within the time set in the chapter or 30 days after the board's final action, whichever is later, according to RSMo 138.430. The statute gives the right to appeal to the Commission from the local board's decision, so the board hearing comes first.

sections.h2: What happens to Dent County land when tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Missouri law sets one statewide sale day for delinquent land, the fourth Monday in August each year (RSMo 140.150). The tax can be paid to the Dent County Collector at any time before the property is sold, including penalty, interest and costs. Call 573-729-3911 for the current sale list and amounts.

  • The Collector mails a first class notice to the publicly recorded owner before the list is published.
  • A second notice goes by certified mail only when the assessed valuation is over $1,000.
  • If the certified notice comes back unsigned, the Collector sends a notice by first class mail to both the owner of record and the occupant.
  • An owner who never received a notice still owes the tax.

A buyer at a tax sale must also give owners and lienholders notice of the right to redeem at least ninety days before acquiring a deed under RSMo 140.405. For an owner of an inherited or vacant house, the practical step is to call the Collector early and learn what is owed.

sections.h2: What is Dent County like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Dent County was organized on February 10, 1851 and takes its name from Lewis Dent, an early settler. It covers 755 square miles, with part of the Mark Twain National Forest and the Ozark National Scenic Riverways inside its borders. Salem, the county seat, had 4,608 people in 2020 and the 1870 Victorian courthouse is on the National Register of Historic Places. Bunker is the other city. Neighbors are Phelps, Crawford, Iron, Reynolds, Shannon and Texas counties.

The county's population was 14,421 in 2020, down from 15,657 in 2010, and the Census Bureau estimates 14,584 for 2025. The county history credits mining and timber, with the old Sligo iron furnace and the lead mines about 30 miles east, and names US Foodservice as the largest employer today. The Census Bureau puts the mean commute at 21.0 minutes and the poverty rate at 14.4%.

School districts in the county are Salem R-80, Dent-Phelps R-III, Green Forest R-II, North Wood R-IV and Oak Hill R-I. Salem also has a Southwest Baptist University annex and a public library. The Census Bureau counted three building permits in the county for 2025. Ask a local title company about recent sales near you.

faqs.q: What is the Dent County property tax due date?
faqs.a: December 31. The Collector mails bills by November 8, and penalty starts on January 1. Call 573-729-3911 if your bill has not arrived.

faqs.q: How do I pay Dent County property tax online?
faqs.a: Use dentcountycollector.com, the portal the Collector's page points to for viewing and paying real estate and personal property statements. You can also pay in person at 400 N. Main Street in Salem, weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

faqs.q: How is residential property assessed in Dent County?
faqs.a: At 19% of market value. Agricultural land is assessed at 12% of production value and all other property at 32% of true value in money. The Assessor reassesses every two years in odd-numbered years and adds new construction each year.

faqs.q: When must a Dent County assessment appeal reach the Board of Equalization?
faqs.a: By the second Monday in July, as RSMo 137.275 provides. The County Clerk at 573-729-4144 schedules the hearings.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to file a personal property list in Dent County?
faqs.a: March 1. Owners list their personal property as of January 1 with the Assessor between January 1 and March 1, and a late list can bring a penalty of up to $105.00. New residents and anyone arriving from another Missouri county need to set up an account.
